elements.name: question75
elements.html:
Protocol: PRA-216-101

Phase: Phase 2a

 

Opening

Thank you for your interest in our Asthma clinical trial. As you may know, asthma is defined as the chronic inflammation of the airways, which can make breathing significantly difficult. Whilst there many inhaled therapies or medication that is widely available, there are still many people living with uncontrolled asthma, signifying the continued need for adequate treatment. As such, Prana Therapeutics have developed a potential new treatment for the management of Asthma.

elements.name: question76
elements.html:
Study drug and design

This study drug is called PRA-216 and will be administered as a subcutaneous injection, likely in the upper arm, abdomen or thigh.. PRA-216 has been designed to stay in the body longer than usual, meaning that recipients of this drug will not need to administer it as frequently. It’s also different to other treatments for asthma as it targets two triggers that set off the condition itself – the chemical signal that releases the allergic response, and the ongoing inflammation.

 

This study intends to assess the effectiveness of this potential new study drug against a placebo. Since the study is double blinded, neither you nor the study team will know which group you are placed into until the end of the trial. You will receive 4 doses of either PRA-216 or the placebo on:

 

  • Day 1
  • Day 15
  • Day 29 
  • Day 85

 

You should allow up to 4 hours for each of these dosing visits.

 

This study is expected to last up to 10 months, consisting of only 14 visits to the facility in Botany.

 

Your first visit will be a “pre-screening” visit, which includes consenting and FeNo testing. You can expect it to last around 30 minutes, unless you require a repeat test, where you can either wait 60 minutes for another test or return to site on another day. Following this, you can expect your screening visit to take up to 3 hours, and you subsequent FU visits to run for around 2 hours.

elements.name: question78
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will be reimbursed for any reasonable travel, parking and other expenses associated with your visits. 

 

You will be reimbursed $455 for each visit that you attend. 

 

Your study schedule consists of a total of 14 in-clinic visits, inclusive of your pre-screening and screening visits.

 

If you attend each scheduled visit, you can be reimbursed up to a total of $6,370.

 

 

Additionally, if you need to return on site for a repeat blood or FeNO test, you will be reimbursed $105 for that visit.

 

You may also require unscheduled visits whilst on the study, which will you will be reimbursed at for $455 per unscheduled visit, on top of the total already mentioned.

 

BREAKDOWN

  • $455 per visit
    • 14 visits
  • Total: Up to $6,370

 

Additional

  • $105 for repeat blood/FeNO test
  • $455 for unscheduled visits

elements.name: question113
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

PARTICIPANTS MUST BE ON A MAINTENANCE THERAPY PRESCRIBED AT LEAST ONCE DAILY - DEFINED AS ICS ALONE (or ICS/LABA and ICS+LAMA)

 

⚠️ If participant has been prescribed an ICS other than at least once daily (e.g. 2-3x per week), they are ineligible.

 

  • Relievers (e.g. Ventolin) are not considered a maintenance therapy
  • Maintenance therapy generally implies a regular ongoing preventer regimen, such as a daily ICS or ICS/LABA

 

⚠️ Please ensure maintenance therapies have been stable for at least 2 months.

⚠️ Please raise medical query if:

 

  • Recent asthma treatment change: Any change in inhaler, tablet, dose or treatment plan in the last 2 months.
  • Asthma exacerbation: Any asthma event requiring a treatment change in the 6 weeks before Screening.
  • Other asthma treatment: Theophylline, regular nebulised bronchodilator therapy, or an asthma medicine not listed above.

  • Allergen immunotherapy: Allergy injections or sublingual immunotherapy with a dose/regimen change in the last 12 weeks, or unwilling to remain stable during the study.

elements.name: question74
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question73
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
